summary: Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1985–1991), where he also served as a research fellow around 1991.
Pieter Hendrik Pott was a Tibetologist, historian, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a curator at Museum Volkenkunde (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.
Pietro Merlo was a linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1868–1872) and under Giovanni Flechia (~1869–1872). He later held a post at the University of Pavia from around 1881 to 1888.

Piotr Balcerowicz is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, the University of Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences. He taught at the University of Warsaw (~1999–2001).

Piotr Klafkowski was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied under teachers including Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, completing his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University under Jerzy Bańczerowski (~1980–1983).

Po-Yao Tien is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (~1990–1995), studying with committee members Rina Sircar and William Stablein (~1993–1995).
Poerbatjaraka was an Indologist, linguist, and historian who studied at Leiden University (~1921–1926). He later held a post at the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964).

Poh Beng Tan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College (~2013–2015) under Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and also studied under teachers Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Polly Young-Eisendrath is a Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her studies at Goddard College (~1967–1969), Ohio University (~1971–1973), and Washington University in St. Louis (~1976–1980).

Pori Park specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (~1995–2000) and served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University (~2001–2007).
Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He has held posts as a professor at the University of Calcutta and at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi studied at Krishnagar Government College and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. An Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist scholar, he held posts at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Prafulla Chandra Ray was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Hare School, Vidyasagar College, Presidency University, and the University of Edinburgh, he held posts at Presidency University (1911–1916) and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture (1916–1936).

Prahlad Pradhan, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, was educated at Patna University and Visva-Bharati. His appointments included posts at Ravenshaw College, Visva-Bharati, Utkal University, Gangadhar Meher University, Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit University.

Pramod Chandra was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Georgetown University (~1951–1953). He held academic posts at the University of Chicago (~1963–1980) and served as a professor at Harvard University (~1980–2003).
Prapod Assavavirulhakarn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Chulalongkorn University (~1990–2016) and served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (~2002–2003).
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Viroj Inthanon and completed a PhD at the University of Mysore by 2014.

Prasenjit Duara is a historian and sinologist educated at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Chicago (~1991–2008) and the National University of Singapore (~2008–2015).
Pratap Kumar Penumala is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (~1996–2017) and as a visiting professor at Colorado College.

Pratapaditya Pal is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and art history. He served as Senior Curator of Indian and Southeast Asian Art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1970–1995) and held a post at the Art Institute of Chicago in 1995.
